Scene: a circular covered record market and neighborhood arcade in an old brick rotunda, early autumn MORNING just before opening. A wide elevated oblique view makes the whole irregular ring of low timber stalls readable around a quiet sunken central listening court, interrupted by four offset passages. Stalls hold milk crates of vinyl with wholly unmarked sleeves, small cassette racks and a few unbranded wood-sided arcade cabinets with gently glowing blue screens. At the center, an old broad tree grows through an open octagonal skylight beside a round listening bench and a turntable with a plain disc. A caretaker is raising one canvas awning and two tiny friends carry a crate through the near gap. Scuffed parquet, brick, faded ochre awnings, dust motes and long shafts of golden morning light, a few curled leaves. Color story: warm honey and burnt terracotta with dark petrol-blue and jade shadows, restrained cream highlights, NOT a generic purple cyberpunk city. Foreground record crates and the curving stall wall frame the full courtyard without obstructing the four passages. The mood is anticipation, shared discoveries and a place returning to life. The loop with four breaks is a narrative echo of Split Ring, not exact authored geometry. No album artwork, no labels, no music-note symbols, no readable cabinet marquees.

Scene: an imagined 1990s suburban transit concourse at RAINY LATE DUSK, built in weathered concrete, smoked glass and enamel-painted steel. One strong diagonal central passage branches into three deep sheltered side halls like a fan; view from an elevated near-left corner so the branching bays remain distinct. Each hall has a different quiet analog gathering place: closest an unbranded arcade repair counter with squat CRT cabinets; middle a listening booth and cassette-deck workbench; farthest a row of waiting benches beside a long rain-streaked window. A single short cream-and-red local train is glimpsed beyond the right window, about to depart; no route boards, maps, timetables or numbers. A tiny traveler carries a portable cassette player, another closes a cabinet door, their figures subordinate to the architecture. A single cable reel and folded repair cloth tell a small story of maintenance after the rush. Color story: inky navy and charcoal, warm sodium orange, crisp muted vermilion columns, very restrained mint-green CRT glow and wet silver reflections. Deep black-blue night outside, no towering futuristic skyline and no violet neon wash. Make the three bays spatially legible, connected by a branching shared spine rather than just a straight row of shopfronts. Mood: the last connection home and quiet work that keeps a shared place alive. Architectural fan only, not collision walls or a controller setup screen.

Scene: an old riverside utility complex converted by a small 1990s music collective into three low rehearsal studios on THREE distinct broad concrete islands, at PALE DAWN after rain. Generous quiet water separates the islands; an aged causeway with missing concrete spans and a few narrow timber-and-steel footbridges connects them in a gentle staggered line across the panorama. Closest island has an open brick listening room with unbranded chunky CRT monitors, an analog synthesizer, plain speakers and a little stack of unlabeled floppy cases; middle island has a glass-roofed rehearsal room and a coiled orange cable; far island has a modest transmitter shed with a rooftop aerial and one warm-lit window. Keep these as three coherent landforms, not many tiny platforms. A low cable crosses along the bridge rail as a subtle thread; it carries no readable signal diagram. Two tiny friends are carrying a keyboard in a hard case over one repaired crossing. Foreground reeds, a battered rowboat and a cup on a concrete step; distant low industrial roofs and soft trees, no vast neon metropolis.
